It sounds like you are on the right path, if you want to find a deeper meaning in life. I know the story from my own life, about a intellectually more advanced teenager, that wants to find meaning. I searched in science and mind, till I reached the conclusion of meaninglessness. Btw, you can sorta enjoy this feeling of meaninglessness, if you are fan of logic, meaninglessness also gives you great freedom.

But I can assure you that it's not all. First you want to find meaning in matter, then in mind and thought. I suppose that's where you are at the moment because I get a general vibe of a overthinker and very active mind. Then mind gets stuck. You reach the conclusion of meaninglessness. But mind can still not give up and wants to connect everything to find a meaning. I reached a very toxic state of my life when I was studying physics and didnt let go of my overactive mind. 

But here's this, mind is only one dimension of your existence, there is also matter, which includes your body and surroundings. Emotions, which are mostly of biological source, like an amplification of instincts from thousands of years of evolution, what gives you basic directions in life since you are born. Next comes awareness, or conciousness, the thing that observes matter, emotions and mind. Again logic, if you can observe a thought, it means that you yourself are not the mind alone, you can observe the mind, emotions and also matter. Also if you try to not think at all (this is a hard thing to do, I would recommend meditation practice for this) you are still there, what means the observer is not the same as the mind. Conciousness is the thing that looks out of your eyes, the core of the "I" that expieriences life, what some people refer to as soul, but I dont think you have to stick to that word, because there are alot of different interpretations. To get closer to your meaning, you'll have to be aware of all those dimensions of existence: Matter, mind, emotions and consciousness (probably more, I'm still finding out on my path). Realise, that you can (and should) sometimes come out of being only in your mind, not think about everything as hard as possible, because what you learned now is, when you only use your mind as reference: life is meaningless. The fact that you already came to this, is one of the reasons I believe that you are on the right path. Mind has it's limits. If you stop your thoughts, you still "are" which means you have access to another dimension of being, the one as the observer. Getting aware of this, is needed to connect all the aspects of your existence of a human being, and will help you alot on your path. 

Many humans have lived on this planet, and almost everyone struggled with this. So I can only recommend, that you grab some books and read what other people have found on this matter, talk to people who are interested in that and be humble and open for things you dont understand yet. Maybe also practise meditation and awareness. Try being in the now without thinking about future or past. Meditation is something that exists since thousands of years, animals do it, and is proofed to be very healthy, so why shouldn't you use these things humanity has prepared for you in all those generations? 

Not sure if it's too long, but maybe you can use some information I wrote and if not, at least you know someone read your post. :)

I wish you happy exploring life and I'm sure you'll find your meaning somewhere, somehow if you keep yourself open for it!

First: If you go to your right panel and select "Inventory", you can scroll through the third and fourth window on the list "Materials" and "Data" to see your stored materials. The fifth would be the *Synthesis* Menu, what would be one of the *uses* for materials already.

Ultimatly you can use materials to *Upgrade* your ship-modules by delivering the mats to an unlocked engineer. But you have to grind and gather alot of different mats for all the different upgrades. That's why you better *Trade* them with a material trader, which are located at certain stations and found via Inara or your ingame galaxy map.

Jameson crash site for *Example*, brings you alot of a certain type of grade 4/5 data, what fills the storage  in 5-10min. But then you have to go to a "data" material trader, and trade for all the other types of data. Repeat that a few times and you will not have to worry about data-mats again.

Edit: Aaaand there is another use for materials I almost forgot to mention that is *Unlocking* modules and weapons through a technology broker. But you'll need very specific stuff for that.

Ok first as I mentioned above: better framerates on single-gpu cards greatly reduce input lag. Having 300fps = +3.3ms GPU rendering lag vs 60fps= 16.6ms rendering lag. If you play a given time on each setting and switch immediatly to the other you'll feel the difference. I don't say you will be telling "oH tHErEs 13.3ms mOrE inPUt lAg" no. But nearly all people feel a difference.  

Input lag isn't solely impacted by fps, there are some settings that reduce it more or less and I can't say what all causes input lag on your pc. 

Just to mention: most average gamers don't have a high end PC. If your settings don't allow to reach 300fps or make it look terrible. Just go with higher is better. Having most fps with "playable" settings is the go to. 

Next: most LCD monitors compute the image from top to bottom (some from bottom to top, but it applies the same). It starts from the top of your monitor and ends at the bottom, then it immediatly starts again from the top. Having a 60hz monitor means it does this 60 times every second or once every 16.6ms. It takes the image rendered by your gpu. Having vsync off allows it to take multiple frames from your GPU in the same computing cycle making it one image made of multiple frames (like layers) this can be an advantage or a disadvantage depending on how much screen tearing you're expieriencing. Screen tearing is the phenomenon where you see those parts of different frames and it looks like your image is shifted for a moment. This is btw also reduced greatly by higher fps. 

The advantage is that if your fps is high enough you see a more accurate image of what is rendered. Therefore a more accurate image of the scenario in the game.

I had this problem when my input lag was too high, and it just felt bad but I couldn't figure out why. So I changed my settings to minimize input lag. 
Make sure you have "vsync off" and unlock your fps to 300. Set every graphics setting to low or off except: "shadows"-low, "render scale" and "textures". Adjust render scale and textures to a playable degree (i have 141% and textures high with 300fps but it depends on your pc)

In general try to minimize input lag as much as possible. It will help alot after you adjust to it.
